claims.quote: Reopening means the auction of an additional amount of an outstanding security.
claims.summary: The term 'reopening' is defined as the auction of an additional amount of an outstanding security.

claims.quote: Security means a Treasury bill, note, or bond, each as described in this part.
claims.summary: The term 'security' is defined as a Treasury bill, note, or bond, each as described in this part.

claims.quote: Security also means any other obligation we issue that is subject to this part according to its auction announcement.
claims.summary: The term 'security' also includes any other obligation issued by the Treasury that is subject to this part according to its auction announcement.

claims.quote: Security includes an interest or principal component under the STRIPS program, as well as a certificate of indebtedness.
claims.summary: The term 'security' includes an interest or principal component under the STRIPS program, as well as a certificate of indebtedness.

claims.quote: Settlement means final and complete payment for securities awarded in an auction and delivery of those securities.
claims.summary: The term 'settlement' is defined as final and complete payment for securities awarded in an auction and delivery of those securities.

claims.quote: Settlement amount means the total of the par amount of securities awarded, less any discount amount or plus any premium amount, and plus any accrued interest.
claims.summary: The term 'settlement amount' is defined as the total of the par amount of securities awarded, less any discount amount or plus any premium amount, and plus any accrued interest.

claims.quote: For inflation-protected securities, the settlement amount also includes any inflation adjustment when such securities are reopened or when the dated date is different from the issue date.
claims.summary: For inflation-protected securities, the settlement amount also includes any inflation adjustment when such securities are reopened or when the dated date is different from the issue date.

claims.quote: Single-price auction means an auction in which all successful bidders pay the same price regardless of the yields, discount rates, or discount margins they each bid.
claims.summary: The term 'single-price auction' is defined as an auction in which all successful bidders pay the same price regardless of the yields, discount rates, or discount margins they each bid.

claims.quote: Spread means the fixed amount over the life of a floating rate note that is added to the index rate in order to determine the interest rate of the floating rate note.
claims.summary: The term 'spread' is defined as the fixed amount over the life of a floating rate note that is added to the index rate in order to determine the interest rate of the floating rate note.

claims.quote: The spread will be determined in the auction of a new floating rate note and is expressed in tenths of a basis point ( i.e. , to three decimals).
claims.summary: The spread will be determined in the auction of a new floating rate note and is expressed in tenths of a basis point (i.e., to three decimals).

claims.quote: Additionally, the spread will be equal to the high discount margin at the time a new floating rate note is auctioned.
claims.summary: Additionally, the spread will be equal to the high discount margin at the time a new floating rate note is auctioned.

claims.quote: STRIPS (Separate Trading of Registered Interest and Principal of Securities) means our program under which eligible securities are authorized to be separated into principal and interest components, and transferred separately.
claims.summary: The term 'STRIPS' is defined as the program under which eligible securities are authorized to be separated into principal and interest components, and transferred separately.

claims.quote: These components are maintained and transferred in the commercial book-entry system.
claims.summary: These components are maintained and transferred in the commercial book-entry system.

claims.quote: Submitter means a person or entity submitting bids directly to us for its own account, for customer accounts, or both.
claims.summary: The term 'submitter' is defined as a person or entity submitting bids directly to the Treasury for its own account, for customer accounts, or both.

claims.quote: Only depository institutions and dealers are permitted to submit bids for customer accounts.
claims.summary: Only depository institutions and dealers are permitted to submit bids for customer accounts.

claims.quote: We permit investment advisers to submit bids on behalf of controlled accounts.
claims.summary: We permit investment advisers to submit bids on behalf of controlled accounts.

claims.quote: TINT means an interest component from a stripped security.
claims.summary: The term 'TINT' is defined as an interest component from a stripped security.

claims.quote: We (or “us”) means the Secretary of the Treasury and his or her delegates, including the Department of the Treasury, Bureau of the Fiscal Service, and their representatives.
claims.summary: The term 'we' or 'us' is defined as the Secretary of the Treasury and his or her delegates, including the Department of the Treasury, Bureau of the Fiscal Service, and their representatives.

claims.quote: The term also includes Federal Reserve Banks acting as fiscal agents of the United States.
claims.summary: The term also includes Federal Reserve Banks acting as fiscal agents of the United States.

claims.quote: Weighted-average means the average of the yields, discount rates, or discount margins at which we award securities to competitive bidders in multiple-price auctions weighted by the par amount of securities allotted at each yield, discount rate, or discount margin.
claims.summary: The term 'weighted-average' is defined as the average of the yields, discount rates, or discount margins at which we award securities to competitive bidders in multiple-price auctions weighted by the par amount of securities allotted at each yield, discount rate, or discount margin.

claims.quote: Yield means the annualized rate of return to maturity on a non-indexed security.
claims.summary: The term 'yield' is defined as the annualized rate of return to maturity on a non-indexed security.

claims.quote: Yield is expressed as a percentage.
claims.summary: Yield is expressed as a percentage.

claims.quote: For an inflation-protected security, yield means the real yield.
claims.summary: For an inflation-protected security, yield means the real yield.

claims.quote: Yield is also referred to as “yield to maturity.”
claims.summary: Yield is also referred to as 'yield to maturity.'

claims.quote: The Treasury Department authorizes Federal Reserve Banks, as fiscal agents of the United States, to perform all activities necessary to carry out the provisions of this part, any auction announcements, and applicable regulations.
claims.summary: The Treasury Department authorizes Federal Reserve Banks, as fiscal agents of the United States, to perform all activities necessary to carry out the provisions of this part, any auction announcements, and applicable regulations.

claims.quote: We offer securities under this part exclusively in book-entry form and as direct obligations of the United States issued under Chapter 31 of Title 31 of the United States Code.
claims.summary: The Treasury offers securities exclusively in book-entry form and as direct obligations of the United States.

claims.quote: When we issue additional securities with the same CUSIP number as outstanding securities, we consider them to be the same securities as the outstanding securities.
claims.summary: The Treasury considers additional securities with the same CUSIP number as outstanding securities to be the same securities.

claims.quote: (1) Are issued at a discount or at par, depending upon the auction results;
claims.summary: Treasury bills are issued at a discount or at par, depending upon the auction results.

claims.quote: (2) Are redeemed at their par amount at maturity;
claims.summary: Treasury bills are redeemed at their par amount at maturity.

claims.quote: (3) Have maturities of not more than one year.
claims.summary: Treasury bills have maturities of not more than one year.

claims.quote: (i) Are issued with a stated rate of interest to be applied to the par amount;
claims.summary: Treasury non-indexed 1 notes are issued with a stated rate of interest to be applied to the par amount.

claims.quote: (ii) Have interest payable semiannually;
claims.summary: Treasury non-indexed 1 notes have interest payable semiannually.

claims.quote: (iii) Are redeemed at their par amount at maturity;
claims.summary: Treasury non-indexed 1 notes are redeemed at their par amount at maturity.

claims.quote: (iv) Are sold at discount, par, or premium, depending upon the auction results;
claims.summary: Treasury non-indexed 1 notes are sold at discount, par, or premium, depending upon the auction results.

claims.quote: (v) Have maturities of at least one year, but of not more than ten years.
claims.summary: Treasury non-indexed 1 notes have maturities of at least one year, but of not more than ten years.

claims.quote: (i) Are issued with a stated rate of interest to be applied to the inflation-adjusted principal on each interest payment date;
claims.summary: Treasury inflation-protected notes are issued with a stated rate of interest to be applied to the inflation-adjusted principal on each interest payment date.

claims.quote: (iii) Are redeemed at maturity at their inflation-adjusted principal, or at their par amount, whichever is greater;
claims.summary: Treasury inflation-protected notes are redeemed at maturity at their inflation-adjusted principal, or at their par amount, whichever is greater.

claims.quote: (iv) Are sold at discount, par, or premium, depending on the auction results (See appendix B for price and interest payment calculations and appendix C for Investment Considerations.);
claims.summary: Treasury inflation-protected notes are sold at discount, par, or premium, depending on the auction results.

claims.quote: (v) Have maturities of at least one year, but not more than ten years.
claims.summary: Treasury inflation-protected notes have maturities of at least one year, but not more than ten years.

claims.quote: (vi) Are only reopened as scheduled or announced.
claims.summary: Treasury inflation-protected notes are only reopened as scheduled or announced.

claims.quote: (i) Are issued with a stated spread to be added to the index rate for daily interest accrual throughout each interest payment period;
claims.summary: Treasury floating rate notes are issued with a stated spread to be added to the index rate for daily interest accrual throughout each interest payment period.

claims.quote: (ii) Have a zero-percent minimum daily interest accrual rate;
claims.summary: Treasury floating rate notes have a zero-percent minimum daily interest accrual rate.

claims.quote: (iii) Have interest payable quarterly;
claims.summary: Treasury floating rate notes have interest payable quarterly.

claims.quote: (iv) Are redeemed at their par amount at maturity;
claims.summary: Treasury floating rate notes are redeemed at their par amount at maturity.

claims.quote: (v) Are sold at discount, par, or premium depending on the auction results (See appendix B for price and interest payment calculations and appendix C for Investment Considerations.);
claims.summary: Treasury floating rate notes are sold at discount, par, or premium depending on the auction results.

claims.quote: (vi) Have maturities of at least one year, but not more than ten years.
claims.summary: Treasury floating rate notes have maturities of at least one year, but not more than ten years.

claims.quote: (iv) Are sold at discount, par, or premium, depending on the auction results;
claims.summary: Treasury non-indexed bonds are sold at discount, par, or premium, depending on the auction results.

claims.quote: (v) Have maturities of more than ten years.
claims.summary: Treasury non-indexed bonds have maturities of more than ten years.

claims.quote: All bids must be submitted using an approved method, which depends on the system into which the awarded securities will be issued. ( See § 356.4.) The approved submission methods for these respective systems are explained in this section. A bidder must provide its assigned bidder identification numbers if it has been assigned one. We have the option of accepting or rejecting incomplete bids.
claims.summary: Bidders must submit bids using an approved method based on the system for awarded securities and provide assigned bidder identification numbers if applicable.

claims.quote: We must receive competitive and noncompetitive bids prior to their respective closing times, which are stated in the auction announcement. We will not include late bids in the auction. For bids other than those submitted on paper forms, our computer time stamp will establish the receipt time. You are bound by your bids after the closing time.
claims.summary: Bidders must submit competitive and noncompetitive bids before their respective closing times as stated in the auction announcement. Late bids will not be included in the auction.

claims.quote: We are not responsible for any delays, errors, or omissions. We are not responsible for any failures or disruptions of equipment or communications facilities used for participating in Treasury auctions.
claims.summary: The Treasury is not responsible for delays, errors, omissions, or failures/disruptions of equipment or communications facilities used in auctions.

claims.quote: Submitters are responsible for bids submitted using computer equipment on their premises, whether or not such bids are authorized.
claims.summary: Submitters are responsible for bids submitted using their own computer equipment, regardless of authorization.

claims.quote: You must have an agreement on file with us under which you agree to our terms and conditions for access to our system for participating in our auctions.
claims.summary: Submitters must have an agreement on file with the Treasury agreeing to the terms and conditions for accessing the system for participating in auctions.

claims.quote: You must submit your bids in accordance with the regulations governing the system in which the security will be held. You may reinvest the proceeds of a maturing security held directly with Treasury as permitted by the system in which it is held.
claims.summary: Bidders must submit bids in accordance with the regulations governing the system in which the security will be held. They may reinvest proceeds of maturing securities held directly with Treasury as permitted by the system.

claims.quote: All bids must state the par amount of securities bid for and must equal or exceed the minimum to bid amount stated in the auction announcement. Bids in larger amounts must be in the multiple stated in the auction announcement.
claims.summary: All bids must state the par amount of securities bid for and must equal or exceed the minimum to bid amount stated in the auction announcement. Bids in larger amounts must be in the multiple stated in the auction announcement.

claims.quote: You may not bid noncompetitively for more than $10 million. The maximum bid limitation does not apply if you are bidding solely through a request to reinvest the proceeds of a maturing security held directly with Treasury, which is a noncompetitive bid.
claims.summary: You may not bid noncompetitively for more than $10 million. The maximum bid limitation does not apply if you are bidding solely through a request to reinvest the proceeds of a maturing security held directly with Treasury, which is a noncompetitive bid.

claims.quote: A competitive bid must show the discount rate bid, expressed with three decimals in .005 increments. The third decimal must be either a zero or a five, for example, 5.320 or 5.325. We will treat any missing decimals as zero, for example, a bid of 5.32 will be treated as 5.320. The rate bid may be a positive number or zero.
claims.summary: A competitive bid must show the discount rate bid, expressed with three decimals in .005 increments. The third decimal must be either a zero or a five, for example, 5.320 or 5.325. We will treat any missing decimals as zero, for example, a bid of 5.32 will be treated as 5.320. The rate bid may be a positive number or zero.

claims.quote: A competitive bid must show the yield bid, expressed with three decimals, for example, 4.170. We will treat any missing decimals as zero, for example, a bid of 4.1 will be treated as 4.100. The yield bid may be a positive number or zero.
claims.summary: A competitive bid must show the yield bid, expressed with three decimals, for example, 4.170. We will treat any missing decimals as zero, for example, a bid of 4.1 will be treated as 4.100. The yield bid may be a positive number or zero.

claims.quote: A competitive bid must show the real yield bid, expressed with three decimals, for example, 3.070. We will treat any missing decimals as zero, for example, a bid of 3 will be treated as 3.000. The real yield may be a positive number, a negative number, or zero.
claims.summary: A competitive bid must show the real yield bid, expressed with three decimals, for example, 3.070. We will treat any missing decimals as zero, for example, a bid of 3 will be treated as 3.000. The real yield may be a positive number, a negative number, or zero.

claims.quote: A competitive bid must show the discount margin bid, expressed as a percentage with three decimals, for example, 0.290 percent. We will treat any missing decimals as zero, for example, a bid of 0.29 will be treated as 0.290. The discount margin bid may be positive, negative, or zero.
claims.summary: A competitive bid must show the discount margin bid, expressed as a percentage with three decimals, for example, 0.290 percent. We will treat any missing decimals as zero, for example, a bid of 0.29 will be treated as 0.290. The discount margin bid may be positive, negative, or zero.

claims.quote: You may not bid competitively in an auction in which you are bidding noncompetitively. You may not bid competitively for securities to be held directly with Treasury.
claims.summary: You may not bid competitively in an auction in which you are bidding noncompetitively. You may not bid competitively for securities to be held directly with Treasury.

claims.quote: If you are bidding competitively in an auction, you must report your net long position when the total of your bids plus your net long position in the security being auctioned equals or exceeds the net long position reporting threshold ( See table.).
claims.summary: You must report your net long position when the total of your bids plus your net long position in the security being auctioned equals or exceeds the net long position reporting threshold.

claims.quote: You must calculate your net long position as of one half-hour prior to the closing time for receipt of competitive bids.
claims.summary: You must calculate your net long position as of one half-hour prior to the closing time for receipt of competitive bids.

claims.quote: If you are a customer and must report either your net long position or a zero, you must report that figure through only one depository institution or dealer.
claims.summary: If you are a customer and must report either your net long position or a zero, you must report that figure through only one depository institution or dealer.

claims.quote: Only depository institutions or dealers may submit bids for customers ( see definitions at
claims.summary: Only depository institutions or dealers may submit bids for customers.

claims.quote: Submitters must remit payment for bids they submit on behalf of customers, including customers of intermediaries, that result in awards of securities in the auction.
claims.summary: Submitters must remit payment for bids they submit on behalf of customers that result in awards of securities in the auction.

claims.quote: Submitters must provide the names of customers whenever they submit bids for them.
claims.summary: Submitters must provide the names of customers whenever they submit bids for them.

claims.quote: For individuals, submitters must provide the customer's full name (first and last).
claims.summary: For individuals, submitters must provide the customer's full name (first and last).

claims.quote: For institutional customers, submitters must provide the name of the institution, and the bidder identification number if the customer provides it.
claims.summary: For institutional customers, submitters must provide the name of the institution, and the bidder identification number if the customer provides it.

claims.quote: For trusts or other fiduciary estates (See appendix A.), submitters must provide on the customer list: (1) The full name or title of the trustee or fiduciary; (2) A reference to the document creating the trust or fiduciary estate with date of execution; and (3) The employer identification number (not social security number) of the trust or fiduciary estate.
claims.summary: For trusts or other fiduciary estates, submitters must provide on the customer list: (1) The full name or title of the trustee or fiduciary; (2) A reference to the document creating the trust or fiduciary estate with date of execution; and (3) The employer identification number (not social security number) of the trust or fiduciary estate.

claims.quote: The submitter must inform a customer of the net long position reporting requirement (See § 356.13.) if the customer is bidding for $100 million or more of securities.
claims.summary: The submitter must inform a customer of the net long position reporting requirement if the customer is bidding for $100 million or more of securities.

claims.quote: If the submitter's or intermediary's personnel know that the customer's position information is not correct, the submitter or intermediary may not submit the customer's bid.
claims.summary: If the submitter's or intermediary's personnel know that the customer's position information is not correct, the submitter or intermediary may not submit the customer's bid.

claims.quote: For each noncompetitive bid, the submitter must provide the customer's name and the amount bid.
claims.summary: For each noncompetitive bid, the submitter must provide the customer's name and the amount bid.

claims.quote: If it provides a summary bid amount, the submitter must transmit the list of individual customers and their bid amounts by close of business on the auction day.
claims.summary: If it provides a summary bid amount, the submitter must transmit the list of individual customers and their bid amounts by close of business on the auction day.

claims.quote: However, the submitter must be able to provide the customer list details by the noncompetitive bidding deadline if requested.
claims.summary: The submitter must be able to provide the customer list details by the noncompetitive bidding deadline if requested.

claims.quote: If it is bidding competitively, an investment adviser must calculate the amount of its bids and positions for purposes of the net long position reporting requirement found in § 356.13(a). In addition to its own competitive bids and positions, the investment adviser must also include in the calculation all other competitive bids and positions that it controls. If the net long position is reportable, the investment adviser must report it as a total in connection with only one bid as stated in § 356.13(a). This requirement applies regardless of whether the investment adviser bids in its own name or in the name of its controlled accounts. The following table shows which positions an investment adviser must include to determine whether it meets the net long position reporting threshold in
claims.summary: An investment adviser must calculate and report its net long position, including all competitive bids and positions it controls, in accordance with § 356.13(a).

claims.quote: If an investment adviser does meet the reporting threshold, the table also shows which positions must be included in, and which may be excluded from, the net long position calculation. If an investment adviser is bidding competitively, and . . . Then . . . (1) the investment adviser has a net long position for its own account that position must be included in the investment adviser's net long position calculation.
claims.summary: The investment adviser must include its own account's net long position in the net long position calculation.

claims.quote: (2) the investment adviser's competitive bid is for a controlled account any net long position of that account must be included in the investment adviser's net long position calculation.
claims.summary: The investment adviser must include the net long position of a controlled account in the net long position calculation.

claims.quote: (3) the investment adviser is not bidding competitively for a controlled account and . . . (i) the controlled account has a net long position of $100 million or more that position must be included in the investment adviser's net long position calculation.
claims.summary: The investment adviser must include the controlled account's net long position of $100 million or more in the net long position calculation.

claims.quote: (ii) the controlled account has a net long position that is less than $100 million that position may be excluded from the investment adviser's net long position calculation.
claims.summary: The investment adviser may exclude the controlled account's net long position if it is less than $100 million.

claims.quote: (iii) any net long position is excluded under paragraph (b)(3)(ii) of this table all net short positions of controlled accounts under $100 million must also be excluded.
claims.summary: If a net long position is excluded under paragraph (b)(3)(ii), all net short positions of controlled accounts under $100 million must also be excluded.

claims.quote: When an investment adviser bids for a controlled account, we deem the investment adviser to have certified that it is complying with this part and the auction announcement for the security. Further, we deem the investment adviser to have certified that the information it provided about bids for controlled accounts is accurate and complete.
claims.summary: The investment adviser must certify compliance with this part and the auction announcement, and that the information provided about bids for controlled accounts is accurate and complete.

claims.quote: Investment advisers that submit competitive bids in the names of controlled accounts are responsible for prorating any awards at the highest accepted yield, discount rate, or discount margin using the same percentage that we announce.
claims.summary: Investment advisers must prorate awards at the highest accepted yield, discount rate, or discount margin using the same percentage announced.

claims.quote: If you submit bids or other information in an auction, we deem you to have certified that: (1) You are in compliance with this part and the auction announcement; (2) The information provided with regard to any bids for your own account is accurate and complete; and (3) The information provided with regard to any bids for customers accurately and completely reflects information provided by your customers or intermediaries.
claims.summary: Submitters must certify compliance with this part and the auction announcement, and that the information provided about bids for their own account and customers is accurate and complete.

claims.quote: If you forward bids in an auction, we deem you to have certified that: (1) You are in compliance with this part and the applicable auction announcement; and (2) That the information you provided to a submitter or other intermediary with regard to bids for customers accurately and completely reflects information provided by those customers or intermediaries.
claims.summary: Intermediaries must certify compliance with this part and the applicable auction announcement, and that the information provided to a submitter or other intermediary regarding bids for customers is accurate and complete.

claims.quote: By bidding for a security as a customer we deem you to have certified that: (1) You are in compliance with this part and the auction announcement and; (2) The information you provided to the submitter or intermediary in connection with the bid is accurate and complete.
claims.summary: Customers must certify compliance with this part and the auction announcement, and that the information provided to the submitter or intermediary in connection with the bid is accurate and complete.

claims.quote: By bidding in an auction, you agree to pay the settlement amount for any securities awarded to you. (See § 356.25.) For notes and bonds, the settlement amount may include a premium amount, accrued interest, and, for inflation-protected securities, an inflation adjustment.
claims.summary: Bidders must agree to pay the settlement amount for any securities awarded to them.

claims.quote: You must pay for your awarded securities by a debit entry to a deposit account that you are authorized to debit or by using the redemption proceeds of your certificate of indebtedness. Payment by debit entry occurs on the settlement date for the actual settlement amount due.
claims.summary: Bidders must pay for awarded securities by a debit entry to a deposit account they are authorized to debit or by using redemption proceeds of their certificate of indebtedness.

claims.quote: payment of the settlement amount must be by charge to the funds account of a depository institution at a Federal Reserve Bank.
claims.summary: Payment of the settlement amount must be made by charging the funds account of a depository institution at a Federal Reserve Bank.

claims.quote: A submitter that does not have a funds account at a Federal Reserve Bank or that chooses not to pay by charge to its own funds account must have an approved autocharge agreement on file with us before submitting any bids.
claims.summary: A submitter without a funds account at a Federal Reserve Bank or choosing not to pay by charge to its own funds account must have an approved autocharge agreement on file with us before submitting any bids.

claims.quote: Any depository institution whose funds account will be charged under an autocharge agreement will receive advance notice from us of the total par amount of, and price to be charged for, securities awarded as a result of the submitter's bids.
claims.summary: Any depository institution whose funds account will be charged under an autocharge agreement will receive advance notice from us of the total par amount of, and price to be charged for, securities awarded as a result of the submitter's bids.

claims.quote: To do this, the following requirements must be met prior to submitting any bids: (i) We must have acknowledged and have on file an autocharge agreement between the clearing corporation and a depository institution.
claims.summary: To instruct delivery and payment through the clearing corporation, the following requirements must be met prior to submitting any bids: We must have acknowledged and have on file an autocharge agreement between the clearing corporation and a depository institution.

claims.quote: We must have acknowledged and have on file a delivery and payment agreement between the submitter and the clearing corporation.
claims.summary: We must have acknowledged and have on file a delivery and payment agreement between the submitter and the clearing corporation.

claims.quote: First we accept in full all non-competitive bids that were submitted by the noncompetitive bidding deadline. After the closing time for receipt of competitive bids we start accepting those at the lowest yields, discount rates, or discount margins, through successively higher yields, discount rates, or discount margins, up to the amount required to meet the offering amount. When necessary, we prorate bids at the highest accepted yield, discount rate, or discount margin as described below. If the amount of noncompetitive bids would absorb all or most of the offering amount, we will accept competitive bids in an amount sufficient to provide a fair determination of the yield, discount rate, or discount margin for the securities we are auctioning.
claims.summary: The Treasury must accept non-competitive bids first, then competitive bids starting from the lowest yields, discount rates, or discount margins, up to the offering amount. If noncompetitive bids absorb most of the offering amount, competitive bids must be accepted to determine the yield, discount rate, or discount margin.

claims.quote: We derive the percentage by dividing the remaining par amount needed to fill the offering amount by the par amount of the bids at the high yield, discount rate, or discount margin and rounding up to the next hundredth of a whole percentage point, for example, 17.13%.
claims.summary: The Treasury must calculate the percentage of bids at the highest accepted yield, discount rate, or discount margin by dividing the remaining par amount needed to fill the offering amount by the par amount of the bids at the high yield, discount rate, or discount margin and rounding up to the next hundredth of a whole percentage point.

claims.quote: If a Treasury non-indexed or inflation-protected note or bond auction results in a yield lower than 0.125 percent, the interest rate will be set at 1/8 of one percent, and successful bidders' award prices will be calculated accordingly.
claims.summary: If a Treasury non-indexed or inflation-protected note or bond auction results in a yield lower than 0.125 percent, the Treasury must set the interest rate at 1/8 of one percent and calculate successful bidders' award prices accordingly.

claims.quote: The interest rate we establish produces the price closest to, but not above, par when evaluated at the yield of awards to successful competitive bidders.
claims.summary: The Treasury must establish an interest rate that produces the price closest to, but not above, par when evaluated at the yield of awards to successful competitive bidders.

claims.quote: The interest rate we establish produces the price closest to, but not above, par when evaluated at the weighted-average yield of awards to successful competitive bidders.
claims.summary: The Treasury must establish an interest rate that produces the price closest to, but not above, par when evaluated at the weighted-average yield of awards to successful competitive bidders.

claims.quote: The interest rate will be the spread plus the index rate (as it may be adjusted on the calendar day following each auction of 13-week bills) subject to a minimum daily interest accrual rate of zero percent.
claims.summary: The Treasury must set the interest rate for floating rate notes as the spread plus the index rate, adjusted on the calendar day following each auction of 13-week bills, subject to a minimum daily interest accrual rate of zero percent.

claims.quote: We round price calculations to six decimal places on the basis of price per hundred, for example, 99.954321
claims.summary: The Treasury must round price calculations to six decimal places on the basis of price per hundred.

claims.quote: We award securities to both noncompetitive and competitive bidders at the price equivalent to the highest accepted yield, discount rate, or discount margin at which bids were accepted. For inflation-protected securities, the price for awarded securities is the price equivalent to the highest accepted real yield.
claims.summary: The Treasury must award securities to both noncompetitive and competitive bidders at the price equivalent to the highest accepted yield, discount rate, or discount margin at which bids were accepted. For inflation-protected securities, the price for awarded securities must be the price equivalent to the highest accepted real yield.

claims.quote: We award securities to competitive bidders at the price equivalent to each yield, discount rate, or discount margin at which their bids were accepted.
claims.summary: The Treasury must award securities to competitive bidders at the price equivalent to each yield, discount rate, or discount margin at which their bids were accepted.

claims.quote: We award securities to noncompetitive bidders at the price equivalent to the weighted average yield, discount rate, or discount margin of accepted competitive bids.
claims.summary: The Treasury must award securities to noncompetitive bidders at the price equivalent to the weighted average yield, discount rate, or discount margin of accepted competitive bids.

claims.quote: We generally prorate bids at the highest accepted yield, discount rate, or discount margin under § 356.20(a)(2) of this part. For example, if 80.15% is the announced percentage at the highest yield, discount rate, or discount margin, we award 80.15% of the amount of each bid at that yield, discount rate, or discount margin. A bid for $100 million at the highest accepted yield, discount rate, or discount margin would be awarded $80,150,000 in this example. We always make awards for at least the minimum to bid, and above that amount we make awards in the appropriate multiple to bid. For example, Treasury bills may be issued with a minimum to bid of $100 and multiples to bid of $100. Say we accept an $18,000 bid at the high discount rate, and the percent awarded at the high discount rate is 88.27%. We would award $15,900 to that bidder, which is an upward adjustment from $15,888.60 ($18,000 × .8827) to the nearest multiple of $100. If we were to award 4.65% of bids at the highest accepted rate, for example, the award for a $100 bid at that rate would be $100, rather than $4.65, in order to meet the minimum to bid for a bill issue. The same prorating rules apply to customers as apply to submitters. Depository institutions and dealers, whether submitters or intermediaries, are responsible for prorating awards for their customers at the same percentage that we announce. For example, if 80.15% is the announced percentage at the highest yield, discount rate, or discount margin, then each customer bid at that yield, discount rate, or discount margin must be awarded 80.15%.
claims.summary: Awards to submitters and customers are calculated by prorating bids at the highest accepted yield, discount rate, or discount margin. The proration percentage is applied to each bid, and awards are made in the appropriate multiple to bid, ensuring at least the minimum to bid is met.

claims.quote: The maximum award to any noncompetitive bidder is $10 million. This limit does not apply to bidders bidding solely through a request to reinvest the proceeds of a maturing security held directly with Treasury. The maximum award is 35 percent of the offering amount less the bidder's net long position as reportable under § 356.13. For example, in a note auction with a $10 billion offering amount, and therefore a maximum award of $3.5 billion, a bidder with a reported net long position of $1 billion could receive a maximum auction award of $2.5 billion. When the bids and net long positions of more than one person or entity must be combined, as is the case with investment advisers and controlled accounts (See § 356.15(c).), we will use this combined amount for the purpose of this 35 percent award limit.
claims.summary: The maximum award to noncompetitive bidders is $10 million, and for competitive bidders, it is 35 percent of the offering amount less the bidder's net long position. When multiple entities are involved, their combined net long positions are used to determine the maximum award.

claims.quote: After the conclusion of the auction, we will make the auction results available on our website at http://www.treasurydirect.gov. The auction results will include such information as: (1) The amounts of bids we accepted and the amount of securities we awarded; (2) The range of accepted yields, discount rates, or discount margins. (3) The proration percentage; (4) The interest rate for a note or bond; (5) A breakdown of the amounts of noncompetitive and competitive bids we accepted from, and awarded to, the public; (6) The amounts of bids tendered and accepted from the Federal Reserve Banks for their own accounts; (7) The bid-to-cover ratio; and (8) Other information that we may decide to include.
claims.summary: Auction results must be made available on the Treasury's website after the auction concludes. The results must include specific information such as accepted bids, awarded securities, accepted yields, proration percentages, interest rates, and bid-to-cover ratios.

claims.quote: We will provide notice to all submitters letting them know whether their bids were successful or not.
claims.summary: The agency must notify submitters whether their bids were successful or not.

claims.quote: We will provide notice of the awards to the clearing corporation that is a party to the agreement.
claims.summary: The agency must notify the clearing corporation that is a party to the delivery and payment agreement of the awards.

claims.quote: You are responsible for notifying them of their awards. You are also responsible for notifying any intermediaries that forwarded successful bids to you.
claims.summary: Submitters are responsible for notifying their customers and intermediaries of their awards.

claims.quote: Similarly, an intermediary is responsible for providing notification of any awards to its customers and any intermedi, from whom it received bids.
claims.summary: Intermediaries are responsible for providing notification of any awards to their customers and intermediaries from whom they received bids.

claims.quote: We will provide notice to each depository institution that has entered into an autocharge agreement with a submitter or a clearing corporation of the amount to be charged, on the issue date, to the institution's funds account at the Federal Reserve Bank servicing the institution. We will provide this notification no later than the day after the auction.
claims.summary: The agency must notify depository institutions with an autocharge agreement of the amount to be charged to their funds account no later than the day after the auction.

claims.quote: Any customer awarded a par amount of $2 billion or more in an auction must send us a confirmation in written form or via e-mail containing the information in paragraph (d)(1)(ii) of this section. The confirmation must be sent no later than 10 a.m. Eastern Time on the next business day following the auction. If sent in written form, the confirmation must be signed by the customer or authorized representative. Confirmations sent by e-mail must be sent by the customer or authorized representative. Confirmations signed or sent by an authorized representative must include the capacity in which the representative is acting.
claims.summary: Customers awarded $2 billion or more must send a confirmation in written form or via e-mail no later than 10 a.m. Eastern Time on the next business day following the auction.

claims.quote: The information the customer must provide is: (A) A confirmation of the awarded bid(s), including the name of each submitter that submitted the bid(s) on the customer's behalf, and (B) A statement indicating whether the customer had a reportable net long position as defined in § 356.13. If a position had to be reported, the statement must provide the amount of the position and the name of the submitter that the customer requested to report the position.
claims.summary: Customers must provide confirmation of the awarded bid(s) and a statement indicating whether they had a reportable net long position, including the amount and submitter if applicable.

claims.quote: A submitter or intermediary submitting or forwarding bids for a customer must notify the customer of the customer confirmation reporting requirement if we award the customer $2 billion or more as a result of those bids.
claims.summary: Submitters or intermediaries must notify the customer of the customer confirmation reporting requirement if the customer is awarded $2 billion or more.

claims.quote: Securities bought in the auction must be paid for by the issue date.
claims.summary: Securities bought in the auction must be paid for by the issue date.

claims.quote: We will charge the settlement amount to the specified account on the issue date.
claims.summary: The agency must charge the settlement amount to the specified account on the issue date.

claims.quote: We will charge the settlement amount to the specified funds account on the issue date.
claims.summary: The agency must charge the settlement amount to the specified funds account on the issue date.

claims.quote: we will redeem the certificate of indebtedness for the settlement amount of the security and apply the proceeds on the issue date.
claims.summary: The party must redeem the certificate of indebtedness for the settlement amount of the security and apply the proceeds on the issue date.

claims.quote: we will pay principal on bills, notes, and bonds on the maturity date as specified in the auction announcement.
claims.summary: The party must pay principal on bills, notes, and bonds on the maturity date as specified in the auction announcement.

claims.quote: we will pay an additional amount so that the additional amount plus the inflation-adjusted principal equals the par amount.
claims.summary: The party must pay an additional amount so that the additional amount plus the inflation-adjusted principal equals the par amount.

claims.quote: we will base the final interest payment on the inflation-adjusted principal at maturity.
claims.summary: The party must base the final interest payment on the inflation-adjusted principal at maturity.

claims.quote: We discharge our payment obligations when we credit payment to the account maintained at a Federal Reserve Bank for a depository institution or other authorized entity, or when we make payment according to the instructions of the person or entity maintaining the account.
claims.summary: The party must discharge payment obligations by crediting payment to the account maintained at a Federal Reserve Bank for a depository institution or other authorized entity, or by making payment according to the instructions of the person or entity maintaining the account.

claims.quote: We discharge our payment obligations when we make payment to a depository institution for credit to the account specified by the owner of the security, when we make payment for a certificate of indebtedness to be issued and held in the owner's account, or when we make payment according to the instructions of the security's owner or the owner's legal representative.
claims.summary: The party must discharge payment obligations by making payment to a depository institution for credit to the account specified by the owner of the security, by making payment for a certificate of indebtedness to be issued and held in the owner's account, or by making payment according to the instructions of the security's owner or the owner's legal representative.

claims.quote: These components must be maintained in the commercial book-entry system.
claims.summary: Components must be maintained in the commercial book-entry system.

claims.quote: The minimum par amount of a non-indexed security that may be stripped is $100. Any par amount to be stripped above $100 must be in a multiple of $100.
claims.summary: The minimum par amount of a non-indexed security that may be stripped is $100. Any par amount to be stripped above $100 must be in a multiple of $100.

claims.quote: Principal components stripped from non-indexed securities are maintained in accounts, and transferred, at their par amount.
claims.summary: Principal components stripped from non-indexed securities are maintained in accounts, and transferred, at their par amount.

claims.quote: Interest components stripped from non-indexed securities have the following features: (i) They are maintained in accounts, and transferred, at their original payment value, which is derived by multiplying the semiannual interest rate and the par amount;
claims.summary: Interest components stripped from non-indexed securities are maintained in accounts, and transferred, at their original payment value, which is derived by multiplying the semiannual interest rate and the par amount.

claims.quote: All interest components with the same maturity date have the same CUSIP number, regardless of the underlying security from which the interest payments were stripped, and therefore are fungible (interchangeable).
claims.summary: All interest components with the same maturity date have the same CUSIP number, regardless of the underlying security from which the interest payments were stripped, and therefore are fungible (interchangeable).

claims.quote: the CUSIP numbers of interest components are different from the CUSIP numbers of principal components and fully constituted securities, even if they have the same maturity date, and therefore are not fungible.
claims.summary: The CUSIP numbers of interest components are different from the CUSIP numbers of principal components and fully constituted securities, even if they have the same maturity date, and therefore are not fungible.

claims.quote: The minimum par amount of an inflation-protected security that may be stripped is $100. Any par amount to be stripped above $100 must be in a multiple of $100.
claims.summary: The minimum par amount of an inflation-protected security that may be stripped is $100. Any par amount to be stripped above $100 must be in a multiple of $100.

claims.quote: At maturity, the holder will receive the inflation-adjusted principal or the par amount, whichever is greater.
claims.summary: At maturity, the holder will receive the inflation-adjusted principal or the par amount, whichever is greater.

claims.quote: Interest components stripped from inflation-protected securities are maintained in accounts, and transferred, at their adjusted value. This value is derived by multiplying the semiannual interest rate by the par amount and then multiplying this value by: 100 divided by the Reference CPI of the original issue date. (The dated date is used instead of the original issue date when the dates are different.) See appendix B, section V of this part for an example of how to do this calculation.
claims.summary: The adjusted value of interest components stripped from inflation-protected securities must be calculated and maintained in accounts, transferred at this value, and an example of the calculation is provided in appendix B, section V.

claims.quote: At maturity, the payment to the holder will be derived by multiplying the adjusted value of the interest component by the Reference CPI of the maturity date, divided by 100. See appendix B, section V of this part for an example of how to do this calculation.
claims.summary: The payment to the holder at maturity for an interest component must be calculated by multiplying the adjusted value of the interest component by the Reference CPI of the maturity date, divided by 100, with an example provided in appendix B, section V.

claims.quote: Stripped interest and principal components may be reconstituted, that is, put back together into their fully constituted form. A principal component and all related unmatured interest components, in the appropriate minimum or multiple amounts or adjusted values, must be submitted together for reconstitution.
claims.summary: Stripped interest and principal components may be reconstituted, and a principal component and all related unmatured interest components must be submitted together for reconstitution in the appropriate minimum or multiple amounts or adjusted values.

claims.quote: Subparts A, B, and D of part 357 of this chapter govern notes and bonds stripped into their STRIPS components, unless we state differently in this part.
claims.summary: Subparts A, B, and D of part 357 of this chapter govern notes and bonds stripped into their STRIPS components, unless otherwise stated in this part.

claims.quote: Securities issued under this part are subject to all applicable taxes imposed under the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, or its successor.
claims.summary: Securities issued under this part are subject to all applicable taxes imposed under the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, or its successor.

claims.quote: Securities issued under this part are exempt from taxation by a State or political subdivision of a State, except for State estate or inheritance taxes and other exceptions as provided in that section.
claims.summary: Securities issued under this part are exempt from taxation by a State or political subdivision of a State, except for State estate or inheritance taxes and other exceptions as provided in that section.

claims.quote: Special federal income tax rules for inflation-protected securities, including stripped inflation-protected principal and interest components, are set forth in Internal Revenue Service regulations.
claims.summary: Special federal income tax rules for inflation-protected securities, including stripped inflation-protected principal and interest components, are set forth in Internal Revenue Service regulations.

claims.quote: Special federal income tax rules for floating rate notes are set forth in Internal Revenue Service regulations.
claims.summary: Special federal income tax rules for floating rate notes are set forth in Internal Revenue Service regulations.

claims.quote: We have the discretion to: (1) Accept, reject, or refuse to recognize any bids submitted in an auction; (2) Award more or less than the amount of securities specified in the auction announcement; (3) Waive any provision of this part for any bidder or submitter; and (4) Change the terms and conditions of an auction.
claims.summary: The Treasury has discretion to accept, reject, or refuse bids, award varying amounts of securities, waive provisions, and change auction terms and conditions.

claims.quote: Our decisions under this part are final. We will provide a public notice if we change any auction provision, term, or condition.
claims.summary: The Treasury must provide a public notice if it changes any auction provision, term, or condition.

claims.quote: If a person or entity fails to comply with any of the auction rules in this part, we will consider the circumstances and take what we deem to be appropriate action. This could include barring the person or entity from participating in future auctions under this part. We also may refer the matter to an appropriate regulatory agency.
claims.summary: The Treasury must consider the circumstances and take appropriate action, including barring non-compliant parties from future auctions and referring matters to regulatory agencies.

claims.quote: If you fail to pay for awarded securities in a timely manner, we may require you to pay liquidated damages of up to one percent of the par amount of securities we awarded to you. Our use of this liquidated damages remedy does not preclude us from using any other appropriate remedy.
claims.summary: A bidder must pay for awarded securities in a timely manner, or face liquidated damages of up to one percent of the par amount of securities awarded.

claims.quote: We consider any persons or entities that intentionally act together with respect to bidding in a Treasury auction to collectively be one bidder.
claims.summary: Persons or entities that intentionally act together in a Treasury auction are considered a single bidder.

claims.quote: Even if an auction participant does not fall under any of the categories listed below, it is our intent that no auction participant receives a larger auction award by acquiring securities through others than it could have received had it been considered one of these types of bidders.
claims.summary: An auction participant must not receive a larger award by acquiring securities through others than it could have received if it were considered one of the listed bidder categories.

claims.quote: A corporation that plans to make use of this exception to the definition of “affiliate” must inform us of this fact in writing and provide the following certification: [Name of corporation] hereby certifies that, with regard to any entity of which it owns more than 50 percent as defined in appendix A to 31 CFR part 356, but for which the purpose of such ownership is to seek a return on investment and not to engage in the business of the entity: • We do not routinely exercise operational or management control over the entity; • We do not exercise any control over investment decisions of the entity regarding U.S. Treasury securities; • We have written policies or procedures, including ongoing compliance monitoring processes, that are designed to prevent the corporation from acting together with the entity regarding participation in Treasury auctions or investment strategies regarding Treasury securities being auctioned; and • We will continue to meet the terms of this certification until we notify the Treasury of a change.
claims.summary: A corporation must inform the Treasury in writing of its intent to use the exception to the definition of 'affiliate' and provide a certification that includes specific conditions regarding ownership, control, and policies.

claims.quote: We may consider a partnership structure that contains one or more corporations as a “partnership” or a “corporation,” but not both.
claims.summary: A partnership structure that contains one or more corporations may be considered either a 'partnership' or a 'corporation,' but not both.

claims.quote: An entity that is more than 50-percent owned as described in this definition is not an affiliate, however, if: • The purpose of such ownership is to seek a return on investment and not to engage in the business of the entity; • The owner does not routinely exercise operational or management control over the entity; • The owner does not exercise any control over investment decisions of the entity regarding U.S. Treasury securities; • The partnership has written policies or procedures, including ongoing compliance monitoring processes, that are designed to prevent it from acting together with the entity regarding participation in Treasury auctions or investment strategies regarding Treasury securities being auctioned; and • The partnership submits notice and certification to us, as provided in this appendix A.
claims.summary: A partnership must submit notice and certification to the Treasury, as provided in appendix A, if it owns more than 50 percent of an entity and meets specific conditions regarding ownership purpose, control, and policies.

claims.quote: A partnership that plans to make use of this exception to the definition of “affiliate” must inform us of this fact in writing and provide the following certification: [Name of partnership] hereby certifies that, with regard to any entity of which it owns more than 50 percent as defined in appendix A to 31 CFR part 356, but for which the purpose of such ownership is to seek a return on investment and not to engage in the business of the entity: • We do not routinely exercise operational or management control over the entity; • We do not exercise any control over investment decisions of the entity regarding U.S. Treasury securities; • We have written policies or procedures, including ongoing compliance monitoring processes, that are designed to prevent the partnership from acting together with the entity regarding participation in Treasury auctions or investment strategies regarding Treasury securities being auctioned; and • We will continue to meet the terms of this certification until we notify the Treasury of a change.
claims.summary: A partnership must inform the Treasury in writing and provide a certification regarding its ownership and control over entities, including written policies to prevent acting together with such entities.

claims.quote: We will consider a government-related entity's fund to be a separate bidder if it meets the definition of the “trust or other fiduciary estate” category, or if applicable law requires that the investments of such fund be made separately.
claims.summary: A government-related entity's fund may be considered a separate bidder if it meets the definition of a trust or other fiduciary estate or if applicable law requires separate investment management.

claims.quote: The trustee or fiduciary must make the decisions on participating in auctions on behalf of the trust or fiduciary estate.
claims.summary: The trustee or fiduciary must make decisions on participating in auctions on behalf of the trust or fiduciary estate.

claims.quote: We consider a person, his or her spouse, and any children under the age of 21 having a common household to be one “individual” bidder.
claims.summary: A person, their spouse, and children under 21 living in the same household are considered one individual bidder.

claims.quote: Such component(s) must be prohibited by law or regulation from exchanging, or must have established written internal procedures designed to prevent the exchange of, information related to bidding in Treasury auctions with any other component in the corporate or partnership structure;
claims.affected_party: component(s) in corporate or partnership structure
claims.summary: Components must be prohibited by law or regulation from exchanging information related to bidding in Treasury auctions with other components, or must have established written internal procedures to prevent such exchange.

claims.quote: Such component(s) must not be created for the purpose of circumventing our bidding and award limitations;
claims.affected_party: component(s) in corporate or partnership structure
claims.summary: Components must not be created for the purpose of circumventing bidding and award limitations.

claims.quote: Decisions related to purchasing Treasury securities at auction and participation in specific auctions must be made by employees of such component(s). Employees of such component(s) that make decisions to purchase or dispose of Treasury securities must not perform the same function for other components within the corporate or partnership structure;
claims.affected_party: employees of component(s) in corporate or partnership structure
claims.summary: Decisions related to purchasing Treasury securities at auction and participation in specific auctions must be made by employees of the component(s). Employees making such decisions must not perform the same function for other components within the corporate or partnership structure.

claims.quote: The records of such component(s) related to the bidding for, acquisition of, and disposition of Treasury securities must be maintained by such component(s). Those records must be identifiable—separate and apart from similar records for other components within the corporate or partnership structure.
claims.affected_party: component(s) in corporate or partnership structure
claims.summary: Records related to the bidding for, acquisition of, and disposition of Treasury securities must be maintained by the component(s) and must be identifiable as separate from similar records for other components within the corporate or partnership structure.

claims.quote: [Name of the bidder] hereby certifies that to the best of its knowledge and belief it meets the criteria for a separate bidder as described in appendix A to 31 CFR part 356.
claims.summary: The bidder must certify that it meets the criteria for a separate bidder as described in appendix A to 31 CFR part 356.

claims.quote: The above-named bidder also certifies that it has established written policies or procedures, including ongoing compliance monitoring processes, that are designed to prevent the component or group of components from: (1) Exchanging any of the following information with any other part of the corporate [partnership] structure: (a) Yields, discount rates, or discount margins at which it plans to bid; (b) amounts of securities for which it plans to bid; (c) positions that it holds or plans to acquire in a security being auctioned; and (d) investment strategies that it plans to follow regarding the security being auctioned, or (2) In any way intentionally acting together with any other part of the corporate [partnership] structure with respect to formulating or entering bids in a Treasury auction.
claims.summary: The bidder must establish written policies and procedures to prevent exchanging specific information with other parts of the corporate structure and intentionally acting together with them in Treasury auctions.

claims.quote: The above-named bidder agrees that it will promptly notify the Department in writing when any of the information provided to obtain separate bidder status changes or when this certification is no longer valid.
claims.summary: The bidder must promptly notify the Department in writing when information provided for separate bidder status changes or when the certification is no longer valid.

claims.quote: we multiply the daily interest decimal by the number of days from, but not including, the issue date to, and including, the first interest payment date.
claims.summary: The issuer must multiply the daily interest decimal by the number of days from the issue date to the first interest payment date.

claims.quote: In cases where the par amount of securities is a multiple of $1,000, we multiply the appropriate multiple by the unrounded interest payment amount per $1,000 par amount.
claims.summary: If the par amount is a multiple of $1,000, the issuer must multiply the appropriate multiple by the unrounded interest payment amount per $1,000 par amount.

claims.quote: we multiply the daily interest decimal by the number of days from, but not including, the issue date to, and including, the last day of the fractional period that ends one full half-year before the interest payment date.
claims.summary: The issuer must multiply the daily interest decimal by the number of days from the issue date to the last day of the fractional period that ends one full half-year before the interest payment date.

claims.quote: We add that amount to the regular interest amount for the full half-year ending on the first interest payment date, resulting in the amount of interest payable for $1,000 par amount.
claims.summary: The issuer must add the calculated amount to the regular interest amount for the full half-year ending on the first interest payment date to determine the interest payable for $1,000 par amount.

claims.quote: In cases where the par amount of securities is a multiple of $1,000, the appropriate multiple should be applied to the unrounded interest payment amount per $1,000 par amount.
claims.summary: If the par amount is a multiple of $1,000, the issuer must apply the appropriate multiple to the unrounded interest payment amount per $1,000 par amount.

claims.quote: We pay interest on marketable Treasury inflation-protected securities on a semiannual basis.
claims.summary: The Treasury must pay interest on marketable Treasury inflation-protected securities on a semiannual basis.

claims.quote: We issue inflation-protected securities with a stated rate of interest that remains constant until maturity.
claims.summary: The Treasury must issue inflation-protected securities with a stated rate of interest that remains constant until maturity.

claims.quote: Interest payments are based on the security's inflation-adjusted principal at the time we pay interest.
claims.summary: The Treasury must base interest payments on the security's inflation-adjusted principal at the time of payment.

claims.quote: We make this adjustment by multiplying the par amount of the security by the applicable Index Ratio.
claims.summary: The Treasury must adjust the par amount of the security by multiplying it by the applicable Index Ratio.

claims.quote: We determine the Ref CPI for any other day of a month by a linear interpolation between the Ref CPI applicable to the first day of the month in which the day falls (in the example, January) and the Ref CPI applicable to the first day of the next month (in the example, February).
claims.summary: The Treasury must determine the Ref CPI for any other day of a month by linear interpolation between the Ref CPI for the first day of the month and the Ref CPI for the first day of the next month.

claims.quote: For interpolation purposes, we truncate calculations with regard to the Ref CPI and the Index Ratio for a specific date to six decimal places, and round to five decimal places.
claims.summary: The Treasury must truncate calculations for the Ref CPI and the Index Ratio for a specific date to six decimal places and round to five decimal places.

claims.quote: If a previously reported CPI is revised, we will continue to use the previously reported (unrevised) CPI in calculating the principal value and interest payments.
claims.summary: The Treasury must continue to use the previously reported (unrevised) CPI in calculating the principal value and interest payments if a previously reported CPI is revised.

claims.quote: If the CPI is rebased to a different year, we will continue to use the CPI based on the base reference period in effect when the security was first issued, as long as that CPI continues to be published.
claims.summary: The Treasury must continue to use the CPI based on the base reference period in effect when the security was first issued, as long as that CPI continues to be published, even if the CPI is rebased to a different year.

claims.quote: We will replace the CPI with an appropriate alternative index if, while an inflation-protected security is outstanding, the applicable CPI is: • Discontinued, • In the judgment of the Secretary, fundamentally altered in a manner materially adverse to the interests of an investor in the security, or • In the judgment of the Secretary, altered by legislation or Executive Order in a manner materially adverse to the interests of an investor in the security.
claims.summary: The issuer must replace the CPI with an appropriate alternative index if the applicable CPI is discontinued, fundamentally altered in a manner materially adverse to the interests of an investor, or altered by legislation or Executive Order in a manner materially adverse to the interests of an investor.

claims.quote: If we decide to substitute an alternative index we will consult with the Bureau of Labor Statistics or any successor agency. We will then notify the public of the substitute index and how we will apply it. Determinations of the Secretary in this regard will be final.
claims.summary: The issuer must consult with the Bureau of Labor Statistics or any successor agency if substituting an alternative index, notify the public of the substitute index and how it will be applied, and ensure that the Secretary's determinations are final.

claims.quote: If the CPI for a particular month is not reported by the last day of the following month, we will announce an index number based on the last available twelve-month change in the CPI. We will base our calculations of our payment obligations that rely on that month's CPI on the index number we announce.
claims.summary: The issuer must announce an index number based on the last available twelve-month change in the CPI if the CPI for a particular month is not reported by the last day of the following month, and base calculations of payment obligations on that index number.

claims.quote: We will calculate interest payments by multiplying one-half of the specified annual interest rate for the inflation-protected securities by the inflation-adjusted principal for the interest payment date.
claims.summary: The issuer must calculate interest payments by multiplying one-half of the specified annual interest rate for the inflation-protected securities by the inflation-adjusted principal for the interest payment date.

claims.quote: We make quarterly interest payments by accruing the daily interest amounts and adding those amounts together for the interest payment period.
claims.summary: The issuer must make quarterly interest payments by accruing the daily interest amounts and adding those amounts together for the interest payment period.

claims.quote: You will have to pay accrued interest on a Treasury bond or note when interest accrues prior to the issue date of the security.
claims.summary: The party must pay accrued interest on a Treasury bond or note when interest accrues prior to the issue date of the security.

claims.quote: You must compensate us through the payment of accrued interest at settlement.
claims.summary: The party must compensate the Treasury through the payment of accrued interest at settlement.

claims.quote: We round all accrued interest computations to five decimal places for a $1,000 par amount, using normal rounding procedures.
claims.summary: The party must round all accrued interest computations to five decimal places for a $1,000 par amount, using normal rounding procedures.

claims.quote: We calculate accrued interest for a par amount of securities greater than $1,000 by applying the appropriate multiple to accrued interest payable for a $1,000 par amount, rounded to five decimal places.
claims.summary: The party must calculate accrued interest for a par amount of securities greater than $1,000 by applying the appropriate multiple to accrued interest payable for a $1,000 par amount, rounded to five decimal places.

claims.quote: We calculate accrued interest for a par amount of securities less than $1,000 by applying the appropriate fraction to accrued interest payable for a $1,000 par amount, rounded to five decimal places.
claims.summary: The party must calculate accrued interest for a par amount of securities less than $1,000 by applying the appropriate fraction to accrued interest payable for a $1,000 par amount, rounded to five decimal places.

claims.quote: However, if at maturity the inflation-adjusted principal is less than a security's par amount, we will pay an additional amount so that the additional amount plus the inflation-adjusted principal equals the par amount. Regardless of whether or not we pay such an additional amount, we will always base interest payments on the inflation-adjusted principal as of the interest payment date. If a security has been stripped, we will pay any such additional amount at maturity to holders of principal components only. (See § 356.30.)
claims.summary: The Treasury will pay an additional amount at maturity if the inflation-adjusted principal is less than the par amount, ensuring the total equals the par amount. Interest payments will always be based on the inflation-adjusted principal as of the interest payment date. If a security has been stripped, the additional amount will be paid to holders of principal components only.

claims.quote: The liquidity of an inflation-protected security may be enhanced over time as we issue additional amounts or more entities participate in the market.
claims.summary: The Treasury may enhance the liquidity of an inflation-protected security over time by issuing additional amounts or encouraging more entities to participate in the market.

claims.quote: Treasury inflation-protected securities and the stripped interest and principal components of these securities are subject to specific tax rules provided by Treasury regulations issued under sections 1275(d) and 1286 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended.
claims.summary: Treasury inflation-protected securities and their stripped components are subject to specific tax rules under sections 1275(d) and 1286 of the Internal Revenue Code.

claims.quote: For a discussion of how we will apply the CPI in various situations, see appendix B, section I, paragraph B of this part. In addition, for a discussion of actions that we would take in the event the CPI is: discontinued; in the judgment of the Secretary, fundamentally altered in a manner materially adverse to the interests of an investor in the security; or, in the judgment of the Secretary, altered by legislation or Executive Order in a manner materially adverse to the interests of an investor in the security, see appendix B, section I, paragraph B.4 of this part.
claims.summary: The Treasury will discuss how the CPI will be applied in various situations in appendix B, section I, paragraph B. It will also discuss actions taken if the CPI is discontinued, fundamentally altered, or altered by legislation or Executive Order in a manner adverse to investors in appendix B, section I, paragraph B.4.
